gloss: to depend on; to act spoiled; to presume upon someone's kindness

definitions.gloss: to depend on someone's affection; to act spoiled; to presume upon someone's kindness
definitions.explanation: To seek or expect indulgence from someone in a close relationship, allowing oneself to be emotionally dependent.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{母親|ははおや}に{甘|あま}えている。
examples.english: The child is acting spoiled with their mother.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{彼|かれ}に{甘|あま}えるのが{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: She's good at acting dependent on him.

examples.japanese: ご{好意|こうい}に{甘|あま}えて、お{言葉|ことば}に{甘|あま}えます。
examples.english: I'll take you up on your kind offer.

notes:
CULTURAL CONCEPT:
{甘|あま}え is a key Japanese psychological concept, famously analyzed by psychiatrist {土居|どい}{健郎|たけお} in his book 「{甘|あま}えの{構造|こうぞう}」(The Anatomy of Dependence). It describes the desire to be passively loved and the expectation of indulgence from close relationships.

TRANSITIVITY:
・Type: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし})
・Pair: {甘|あま}やかす (to spoil, to pamper) - transitive
・Pattern: XがYに{甘|あま}える

ASPECT:
・{甘|あま}えている = is currently acting dependent/spoiled (ongoing action or state)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・Xに{甘|あま}える (to depend on X, to act spoiled toward X)
・{好意|こうい}に{甘|あま}える (to take advantage of someone's kindness)
・お{言葉|ことば}に{甘|あま}えて (taking you up on your kind words - polite acceptance)
・{親切|しんせつ}に{甘|あま}える (to presume upon someone's kindness)

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {甘|あま}えっていませんでした
